subject: 4PH1
skill: Convert a supplied mass in grams to kilograms and evaluate weight using the supplied formula and stated gravitational field strength.

customQuiz.rationale: Preserves the original substitution/evaluation structure and gram conversion. An explicitly fixed g and table presentation are adaptations; method-credit, power-of-ten and rounding responses need calibration before use.

requirements: Original load context with one positive mass stated in grams.
Supply W = mg and state one g value explicitly; no gravitational lookup required.
Ask for weight, not net force, mass or support force.
evidenceContract: Freeze mass in integer grams and g in integer hundredths of N/kg.
Store exact decimal mass/weight and source-specific rubric notes privately.
Public question contains only the givens, prompt and maximum marks.

constraints: Strictly positive and a multiple of five grams; input is never already in kg.
Only the discrete values 980, 981 and 1000 are allowed, representing 9.8, 9.81 and 10 N/kg.
Equivalent mass and field-strength readings appear in either form.
Select one original generic load context; no extra mechanical model or forces are implied.
No inverse task, buoyancy, changing g, zero mass or resultant-force calculation in this version.
Do not change the original two-mark source into a three-mark unit/conversion/method scheme.
Never activate from arithmetic checks alone.
difficultyControls: Vary conversion and decimal multiplication values without claiming equal difficulty.
Prose/table presentation changes reading demand and remains provisional.

transformations.conditions: Stay inside the explicit gram domain and recompute exact solution.
The original scheme allows several g values; generated prompts explicitly select one. Calibrate this change rather than copying the original acceptance list blindly.
All quantities and units must match the same frozen parameters.
Mass or g as the target requires a separate demand/rubric review.

solutionProcedure: Convert the stated mass from grams to kg.
Substitute the converted mass and the stated g into W = mg.
Evaluate and report weight in N, retaining suitable precision.

criteria.rule: Substitution into W=mg; a clear power-of-ten mass conversion error is handled by the source's one-mark deduction rule.
Correct evaluation using the stated g, with method and single-error handling calibrated before serving.

acceptableAlternatives: Equivalent decimal working; exact generated answers are stored privately.
Original Q10(a) additionally accepts g=9.8/9.81 and resulting 2.45/2.4525 N for its 250 g load. These are source observations, not automatic alternatives to a generated explicitly stated g.
dependencies: Source scheme ignores units and deducts one mark for a clear power-of-ten error in mass units; avoid repeated penalties for the same error.
A plausible wrong number alone cannot establish a power-of-ten method without supporting working.
contradictionRules: The offline explicit-product marker defers additional working, competing claims, inconsistent final answers and unsupported notation. It does not parse free-text solutions or infer missing working.

tolerance.roundingRule: Exact decimal model supplied. Acceptable rounded responses and implied method credit remain uncalibrated; do not automatically reject rounded work or serve this provisional rubric.

commonErrors.description: Using a gram reading as though it were kilograms.
Dividing by g instead of multiplying for weight.

testPlan: 200 deterministic seeds; both representations, all g values and all contexts.
Independent exact-answer fixtures including original permitted g values, unit boundaries and decimal cases.
Reject altered public/private content, unsupported g, mass boundaries and activation flags.
Before promotion calibrate method/ECF, clear power-of-ten errors, units, rounding, contradictory answers and complete final-answer-only responses.
36 hand-authored explicit-product response fixtures: exact evaluation, method-only, one mass power-of-ten deduction and conservative review routing. Not real-student calibration.

runtime.seedPolicy: Unsigned 32-bit seed; bounded deterministic integer parameters. Store full validated package before any future serving; no live integration.

blockers: Arithmetic checks pass for 200 seeds, 108 boundary/context cases and 12 independent-answer/presentation fixtures; pedagogical validation remains incomplete.

A bounded offline explicit-product marker passes 36 synthetic fixtures (20 scored, 16 deferred). Rounding, implied method, competing working, arbitrary errors and free-text interpretation remain uncalibrated.
Explicit g and prose/table adaptations have a recorded source-demand review but no empirical difficulty equivalence; alternative-g answers are deferred.
Official per-task AO allocation unverified; not registered for live sessions.
